text:
I'm a freshman at a Tennessee university and have recently learned I might be considered a person of interest (POI) by campus police, allegedly for xanax selling. For background: I have ADHD, depression, and anxiety, and am prescribed adderall, alprazolam, an antidepressant, and an atypical antipsychotic, all of which I keep locked up. All my meds are legal and prescribed by a reputable psychiatrist. 

I have no criminal record, no disciplinary history, and no history of misusing meds. I cooperated with campus police in the past (reporting safety issues, helping friends, etc.), and have always tested negative for any drugs not prescribed to me. 

A friend saw my name listed as a POI for xanax selling in the campus police department. I have never sold my medication and have not done anything illegal, but now I'm anxious. 

Given the situation, should I contact a lawyer just in case, or is it better to do nothing and carry on as usual since I haven’t broken any laws? What steps, if any, should I take to protect myself or clear up the situation?

I started working for my current employer nearly 2 months ago as their first and only part-timer (I’m still in college). They’re paying me as agreed and things seem fine, but I haven’t signed a contract yet. Every time I ask HR about it, she says their lawyer is still working on the contract since this is a new situation for them. What risks do I face by working without a signed contract?

I work in Illinois and I’ve been making $9.00 an hour for 5 months, but I saw the state minimum wage just went up to $9.25 on New Year’s Day. What steps do I need to take to make sure my employer pays me the new minimum wage? Any guidance on how to bring this up or what my rights are would help.

I’m a Minnesota landlord and have a question about security deposits. I bought a duplex last year and live in the lower unit. The upper unit tenants have been there for 4-5 years and their lease with the previous owner didn't mention smoking, though the previous owner verbally said the building was non-smoking. When they signed a new lease with me, it specifically designated the unit as non-smoking. 

Even though the lease says no smoking, the tenants definitely smoke indoors and I can smell it, but it doesn’t bother me much since there’s no carpeting and the smell doesn’t affect the rest of the building. If they move out when their lease ends in May, I’d need to repaint the entire 1300sqft unit (walls and ceiling) to get rid of the smoke smell. I have an $850 security deposit from them. Based on Minnesota law, do I have reasonable grounds to deduct the cost of repainting due to the smoke smell, considering it's a violation of the lease and not ordinary wear and tear?

I've been going to a private gym under contract, $9.00/month for 1 year, payments set up by EFT from my own account after I turned 18 (my dad signed for me originally, but charges should go to me now). Only the first payment showed up; after that, I haven’t seen deductions, even though the contract says they can collect all dues and add late or service fees if any payment is late. The club uses ABC Financial for billing. If payments aren't coming out, am I on the hook for extra late and service fees or is this on them? How should I handle this situation?

EDIT: Just saw he actually has been taking out payments but missed a month or two—will skipping a month or two be an issue for me, or could there be extra fees?

I'm a 20-year-old woman in England and need advice on claiming back tax that was wrongly deducted from my pay. Last year I worked three jobs (nightclub, bar, and hotel). At the bar, my paperwork was late, so I got taxed about £200 before HMRC had the right info.

HMRC told me I'd get the money back in a few weeks, but I never received it—even after the tax year ended. When I called again, they said my hotel employer hadn't submitted my P60 form, and I'm apparently still on their payroll even though I haven’t worked there in almost a year.

After COVID hit, I lost all my jobs and couldn’t pay rent. I asked my hotel boss for my P60 so I can claim the tax back. She said she'd email it but never did, and now she's ignoring my messages. The hotel is a small business so there isn’t anyone else I can contact.

How can I get my P60 or my tax refund if my ex-employer won’t help? Is there a way for HMRC to sort this without my boss? I really need the £200 and would appreciate any advice on what to do next.

A New Jersey estate question: When a deceased person leaves their residence to a beneficiary but there is a rent-free occupant living above the garage, is it the executor's responsibility to handle eviction of that occupant before the estate is settled and the property is transferred? The executor in this case is the attorney, and the beneficiary lives out of state. The occupant has refused to pay despite having the means. Who is responsible for the eviction?

How should I answer the "Did you end a job?" question for Unemployment in North Carolina if I was laid off due to Covid-19, was asked to return after 6 weeks, requested a bit more time for safety, and was then fired for "refusing to work"?

My homeroom teacher in Victoria, Australia is enforcing a system where if students are late, have their shirt untucked, swear, or break other classroom rules, we have to pay a “fine.” The amount is decided by rolling a dice—possible amounts range from $0.00 up to double the next roll—with the money supposedly going to charity. This only applies to my class (24 students out of 1200), while the rest of the school isn’t fined for the same infractions and usually just receives a detention if punished at all. Is it legal for a teacher to require students to pay money like this when charity donations are supposed to be voluntary? Looking for advice on this situation.

My partner’s father died by suicide over two months ago in a small Minnesota town and the death certificate still hasn’t been issued. The body was sent to Minneapolis for autopsy, and both the sheriff’s office and the funeral home say they’re waiting for the doctors. We need the certificate for legal matters like stopping foreclosure and accessing funds. We live out of state and have only been able to call the sheriff’s office. Is this long of a wait for the death certificate after a suicide normal in Minnesota, and is there legal action we can take to speed it up?

I want to write a critical article about a large Chinese e-commerce company that has a bad reputation in my community for shady business practices, even though they look good in Google results. My blog ranks well on Google and I’d like to publish honest negative feedback to help others, but I don’t want to risk any legal trouble (like defamation). Most of my info is from community reports, complaints, and some personal experience, not hard evidence. I’m based in Florida, USA, and the company is in Shenzhen, China. What legal issues should I be aware of before publishing something like this?

I need to write a letter to a judge about my ex spouse, who strangled me in front of our children. The ex accepted a plea in abeyance but didn't complete it. At their sentencing hearing, their lawyer said there was a clerical error, so the judge gave them more time to finish the plea. For months, there's been a court day every first Thursday, called evidentiary hearings, about the strangling incident. I'm upset about the judge's decision and the leniency, because my ex is still harassing, stalking, and trying to control me, and the abuse continues. I don't have a lawyer, so I need advice—especially since the court needs to know the ongoing abuse is related to the strangling. The perpetrator has even stalked and harassed my new partner. I need help.

I was fired from my warehouse job in Illinois for “unprofessional behavior in the workplace” after a brief heated argument with a supervisor. The argument happened off the clock, outside the building, and involved raised voices but no physical altercation. I’ve filed for unemployment and expect it to be contested as misconduct.

I did not previously receive any warnings or disciplinary actions at this job, which is known for high turnover and a toxic environment. I have a diagnosed bipolar disorder (made known to the employer) that impacts my control over my temper, especially in stressful situations.

According to Illinois law, misconduct requires a “deliberate and willful violation” of a reasonable rule, with damage to the employer or repeat offenses after a warning. The incident didn’t occur during working hours or inside the workplace, and there’s no history of prior warnings. I’m unsure whether to mention my mental health diagnosis in my claim.

Given these facts, what are my chances of qualifying for unemployment benefits, and what should I expect during the process?

My wife was pulled over in Wichita, Kansas for having expired tags that were 29 days overdue. The officer also saw that the license plates were on an unregistered vehicle due to a mix-up when the car was transferred from her parents. She got a court date instead of a regular fine. We're not sure what happens in court for something like this and her court appearance is tomorrow. Can you give a brief idea of what to expect or how to prepare, since neither of us has handled this kind of situation before?

I'm in the middle of a separation with my wife and we're working out child custody. We're splitting physical custody of our kid but she insists on having sole legal custody. I'm really hesitant to agree and she's threatening court action if I don't go along with it.
Can having a clear, understandable motive lead to a reduced sentence for a killing?

Can a landlord in Pennsylvania get in legal trouble for showing a rental apartment to potential tenants if the smoke detectors aren't currently installed, but there's a clear disclaimer that repairs and installations—including smoke detectors—will be completed before move-in? Previous tenants removed the smoke detectors and left one on the counter, and the property is under active cleanup with repairs scheduled. Could showing the unit in this state be considered illegal, or is it only a problem if smoke detectors are missing at the time of occupancy?

My former landlord is asking me to pay $940 for damages after moving out. Our lease ended 21 days ago, but I actually moved out 3 months back with her knowledge due to two break-ins she did nothing about. There was a small hole left in the wall when I moved out, but now she sent me a detailed repair estimate, including extra costs for custom trim. Can I request a different quote or get my own? I read the Goodeill vs. Madison Real Estate case, which said an estimate isn’t good enough within certain days, and I checked the relevant Kansas statute but I’m confused. Would appreciate help on understanding my rights here.

[Kansas Legislation](http://www.kslegislature.org/li_2012/b2011_12/statute/058_000_0000_chapter/058_025_0000_article/058_025_0108_section/058_025_0108_k/)

[Goodeill vs. Madison Real Estate](https://www.courts.wa.gov/opinions/pdf/324427.pub.pdf)

I'm an immigrant teacher in the US with a work visa. Recently, a detective contacted me because I’ve been accused of something, though I don’t know what. I’m hiring a lawyer to help clear my name, and I trust the truth will come out.

My concern is what happens after I’m proven innocent and if the case is determined to be defamation or a false accusation. I’m worried my employer or school district might still decide not to rehire me, even though I would be the victim. I’ve heard from some lawyers that this is a real possibility, but I also know of a teacher who returned after being on leave.

What are my rights as an immigrant worker in this situation? Can my employer fire me just because I was accused, even if I did nothing wrong and am cleared by the investigation? Does the law allow this kind of termination? Is there legal protection for immigrant workers who are cleared of false accusations, and are there lawyers who defend people like me in these cases?

I want to know if it’s true that I could lose my job and career, even though I’m innocent. What recourse do I have, and what options are available to me as an immigrant worker in this scenario?

I signed a Settlement and Release Agreement with my former employer after leaving due to an unsafe work environment (in Nova Scotia, Canada). Payment was arranged through the Labour Board: the cheques were sent to them, then handed over to me once cleared, and we both signed the settlement agreement. I cashed three cheques in early April. Afterward, I started a Peace Bond process separately. Following the first hearing, the employer emailed me saying they would cancel the cheques. 

Is it possible for them to cancel or reverse the cheques after we both signed the Settlement and Release Agreement and the Labour Board was involved? What should I do next?

Signed a letter of intent to start a new job on June 1, but considering backing out. My current job is stressful, but the new one seems easier with less responsibility. I’ve been cleared for escort entry, but I’m worried I might not get fully cleared and could lose the offer. No criminal record or anything, just feeling paranoid. Are there any consequences for withdrawing from a signed letter of intent in Virginia?

My apartment complex garage has had multiple theft incidents: about 5 months ago, 20 luxury cars had airbags stolen during a break-in where the garage gate was opened maliciously. Management said they couldn't install cameras due to COVID-19 but have had other contractors renovating the pool and common areas since then. Yesterday, my insured motorcycle was stolen overnight; management told me the gate was prevented from closing by tape on the sensor. The lease says they're not liable for theft or required to provide security, but they charge us extra for fob access and enclosed parking. Given repeated incidents and no added protections, could this be considered negligence by management?

My employer in Illinois closed due to COVID, and after the shutdown, sent an email saying: “All back pay will be paid in full once we have been approved for the SBA disaster loan or business resumes as usual (whichever comes first).” The office closed on 3/16 and we had a pay period due, but they delayed paychecks. Since then, we haven’t had updates on the SBA loan and were recently told business won’t resume until late summer/early fall—still no mention of checks.

Is it legal for them to withhold paychecks in this situation? Can they delay payment if they’ve applied for an SBA disaster loan, or are they required to pay per Illinois law? I’m aware of 820 ILCS 115/4, which sets pay deadlines after a pay period and says employers must pay all wages no later than the next regular payday after a layoff. I’ve drafted an email demanding unpaid wages but want to be sure they’re not somehow protected in this scenario before I send it.

Explain how child support works in Mississippi, especially in complicated cases. Here’s my situation: two years ago, I was sexually assaulted while unconscious by a woman who later got pregnant. I felt ashamed, so I didn’t report anything and we agreed I’d pay her $300/month directly (not through the state). Later, she wanted to put the child up for adoption and I tried to help with that, but the adoption didn’t happen. Then I got an official letter requiring me to go to court. When I called the number, they said I didn’t actually have to go and they’d send a paternity test kit for me to return. I never got that kit, and months later, a new letter arrived saying the state was opening a child support case against me. When I called, they said there was no record. The woman is now asking for $600/month—which I can’t afford—then said we could agree to $400/month. Now she claims the state also requires me to cover her car payment and insurance, and that non-custodial parents in Mississippi are legally required to do this. She says I can just pay her the $400 support plus $165 for insurance. I can’t find any law about car payments or insurance being required in Mississippi. I’m trying to save for a lawyer, but I’m running out of money fast. What is the actual law here, and what are my options?

My mom owns a business in Miami, Florida and brought on her long-time friend as a partner. The friend quickly became invasive, constantly demanding to know my mom’s whereabouts, asking for her passwords, and trying to break into her phone when my mom left it unattended at the store (she’d return to "too many failed attempts" lockout screens). Things escalated—her friend cursed her out and told her to leave the store, then later tracked her down in the shopping center and harassed her, showing printed out emails and text messages from my mom’s account. My mom never gave her password or permission to access these. The friend’s son works for T-Mobile, which might be how she got access to the text messages, but I’m not sure. My mom is feeling overwhelmed and I want to know what steps we can take, both legally and practically, to protect her given this situation. Any guidance for next actions in Florida would be appreciated.

A friend signed a one-year Massachusetts rental lease, paid first, last, and security, but left after three days because their dogs didn't get along. They don’t expect to get their deposit back, but now the landlord still wants to hold them to the lease. Is there any kind of early termination clause or exception for such a short stay, under a week? Can the landlord take legal action to enforce the lease in this situation? Looking for advice on what options exist.

Last week at my gymnasium in Estonia, we were required to attend a mandatory assembly that was advertised as a talk about healthy eating. Instead, it turned out to be a presentation promoting a multi-level marketing scheme centered around the Vemma drink. The speakers tried to convince us that the product would improve our lives and encouraged participation. I’m wondering: is it legal for schools to allow MLM advertising like this, especially targeting minors during compulsory school hours? If not, who would be responsible for allowing it?

In California, what’s the legal process for evicting a family member who has been living in my home without a rental agreement? My mother has lived with my wife and me since August, but she has become destructive, smokes inside despite health concerns, damages property, and consistently breaks house rules. We’ve given her notice to move out by the end of October and are willing to offer her $400 a month for a year if she leaves and doesn’t return. If she refuses, do we need to go through formal eviction proceedings to legally remove her?

My dorm room in Wisconsin had a ceiling leak due to a burst pipe (caused by residents above leaving their window open in freezing weather), which damaged my textbooks and got water all over my room. Security and a hall director saw the damage, took our names, and we both documented everything with photos. Despite making reports and asking for help with cleanup, my roommate and I ended up handling most of the cleaning ourselves, and the situation repeated again the next day. It’s been two weeks with no follow-up or offers of compensation from the school. Are they responsible for compensating us for damaged property? If so, who should I contact to pursue this, since no one has reached out?

Explain the legal definition of "distribution" and outline any risks to the end receivers ("Ned receivers") under US and New Hampshire law.

If a law imposes penalties specifically on those who "produce" or "distribute" a product, does the person who buys or consumes the product face any legal risk? My understanding is that end receivers would not be penalized if merely possessing the product is not illegal, but I haven’t been able to find definite statutory wording to confirm this. 

Let me know if I’ve missed something regarding forum guidelines.

I'm an appliance technician in Texas, 22 years old. I signed a contract without reading it and later realized it says I can't own an appliance company, work for another appliance company, or do appliance repair at all for five years if I quit. Are there any loopholes or ways around this?

I lived in Iowa and shared an apartment with a friend in college. While I was away for summer break, my roommate sublet his room to someone else without telling me, and the apartment complex didn’t notify me either. When I returned, there was a stranger living there who ended up causing significant damage. Because of this, I moved out a couple of months early and stopped paying rent, expecting my deposit to cover the damages. It’s been about 8 years since then, but now something has shown up on my credit report saying I owe money to a collections agency after I applied for a new apartment. What’s the best way to handle this, and is there any way I can get this removed from my credit report without paying?

If I make a single prank call to someone in Palo Alto, CA, pretending to be someone involved with their patent (not actually claiming to be a patent officer, just someone looking at their patent), could I get arrested for that? The person I called was someone I used to work with (no contract, never paid, recently found out I was removed from their website along with another band member, no notice given). I regret the call—he knows my address and my parents’ phone numbers, and I'm anxious about what could happen next. Would one prank call like this get me in legal trouble? More details available if needed.

My landlords (who are my roommate’s parents) want me to move to a new property they found because they want to sell the current one. I live in Lincoln, Nebraska, and signed a one-year lease with them in May 2014. The lease does not mention anything about being asked to move properties. It is now five months into the lease. My roommate just texted me that her parents expect us to move to this new house. I have not agreed to move. Does them expecting me to move to a different property mean the lease is void?

My mom and her ex-husband (my former stepdad) co-own a house in Louisiana. They divorced while he was in jail, and there was no property settlement during the divorce. My mom kept paying the mortgage alone while he was incarcerated. Now, he owes both of us money (we helped him financially after he got out), but he refuses to sell the house or buy out my mom’s share. Is there a legal way to force a sale or require him to buy her out of the property?

CT traffic ticket – hired a lawyer, outcome worse than before. 

Got a stop sign ticket while using my phone for GPS. Officer cited me for the stop sign, not the phone, but I already had 2 prior speeding tickets last year (I’m under 25), so if I got one more moving violation, my license would be suspended even after doing operator retraining. I hired a lawyer hoping to avoid the penalty and the insurance hit. First court date, prosecutor wouldn’t drop it. Lawyer suggested pleading guilty to a cell phone violation instead, claiming since I had no prior cell phone offenses it wouldn’t cause a suspension – just a higher fine. Prosecutor agreed. Pleaded guilty as advised.

Now I got notice my license is being suspended anyway. Lawyer took days to get back to me and finally said it’s because any violation after retraining means suspension, regardless of type. This is opposite of what he told me earlier. I feel like I got bad advice and paid $500 just to be in a worse position. Is it reasonable to ask for my money back? If not, should I file a complaint with the bar? What’s the best course of action now?

My husband and I are getting divorced in Michigan and living in a mobile home park, month-to-month lease after five years here. He says he can’t move into his new place until he’s off our current lease and wants me to fill out a solo application, but I can’t afford it or qualify until child support begins. He’s communicating with the owner behind my back and threatening eviction if I don’t cooperate. 

Can another tenant (my husband) force me to sign a new lease, break the current lease, or sell the mobile home without my consent, or otherwise force me out?

Got a speeding ticket in Pennsylvania: pulled over for 79 in a 55, but the officer reduced it and wrote me up for 60 in a 55 so no points, just the fine. Radar device was tested on 12/22/2014. Fine is $35 but with all the added fees (E.M.S., Surcharge, J.C.P., A.T.J.) the total is $138.50. First offense, want to keep my record clean, but not sure if it’s worth trying to fight since it was already reduced. If I just pay it, will my insurance go up even though there are no points? Should I fight it or just pay?

[PA/NY] Gave up biological child for adoption to relatives 10 years ago; now adoptive parents want us to take him back due to his severe special needs (nonverbal autism, not toilet trained, etc). Adoption was supposed to be semi-open, but we’ve only seen him twice at family events. Lately, adoptive parents are messaging and calling, saying we need to “take responsibility” and contribute more because he “isn’t normal”—even suggesting he may need to live with us. We can’t afford his care, and he was legally adopted by them as a baby. What is our legal obligation? Stopped responding to avoid creating an agreement or expectation—concerned about being required to help.

My lease contract says last month's rent was prepaid and is on deposit, along with my security deposit. Now, as I’m moving out, my property manager says that’s a typo and I still have to pay last month’s rent, even though it’s written on the agreement (the written amount is also $70 less than my regular rent). I don’t remember if I ever actually paid last month’s rent up front, but since it’s in the contract, do they have the right to make me pay again or for a different amount? What rights do I have here in St. Louis, MO?

I stayed temporarily with someone in Sweden who offered me free accommodation for a few days (Jan 18–23) but then demanded 500 SEK under threat of withholding my belongings, even though there was no rental contract and I had a Facebook message stating it would be free. The landlord confirmed he would only have charged 166 SEK and electricity was already included in the rent. I paid because my personal property (computer, university work, etc.) was at stake.

Reasons given for demanding payment included minor things like storing food in the fridge without explicit permission and similar petty complaints. I have Facebook chat copies showing permission to stay for free but was later blocked and can’t recover all conversations. I also have several witnesses and support from the landlord. No receipt was given for money paid. What steps can I take, legally or otherwise, about this extortion?

Here’s an update on my previous issue about the dangerous stairs at my apartment complex in Virginia. I followed advice and contacted the local code office with an email and photos. They responded quickly and promised an inspection.

Yesterday I got home to find a notice taped to my building about the stairs. After calling the code office, I learned the closure only applied to the broken stairwell, so I wasn’t locked out. When I stopped by the leasing office later, staff were holding an emergency meeting because other residents were upset. The management said a contractor was coming in that day to repair the stairs and inspect for more issues, so the county would eventually remove the warning sign.

Thanks to the advice I got, the problem is being addressed. Mission accomplished.

I've got a Magistrates court appearance next week in Adelaide for a speeding ticket. I was going to contest it but don’t have any evidence to fight the charge, so now I’m planning to talk to the prosecution and try to get a reduced penalty or cut a deal. I’ve never been to court before and have no idea what to expect or what I should say. Can you give me some advice or tips for what to do in this situation?

20-year-old full-time college student in Albany, NY. Moved out of my mother’s house in October 2019 due to mental health reasons and now live with my grandparents. My biological father still pays child support to my mother, even though she told him I no longer live with her. I understand support continues until I turn 21 because I’m a full-time student, but my grandparents and I are frustrated that my mother is still receiving it even though I’m not her dependent. Is there a way for me to receive the child support payments instead?

[California] Full-Time employee reduced to 16 hours/week but still considered Full-Time on paper. Employer encouraged filing for Unemployment. Is this fraud?

Employer cut our hours from 40 to 16 per week due to COVID and told us to file for unemployment, but said we’re still “Full-Time” on paper so we keep our benefits. There’s no HR department to get answers from. We suspect this might be related to PPP loan requirements.

Questions:
1. Will being labeled Full-Time while my hours are reduced affect my eligibility for unemployment?
2. Do employees need to be listed as Full-Time for the business to qualify for the PPP loan?

Had a hypothetical situation: I rear-ended a driver today because I was following too closely and he slammed on his brakes in traffic. There was only minor damage to his truck, so he didn’t want compensation, but my car got a hole in it and the hood is popped up, though still drivable. Nobody was hurt. While talking to the other driver, I realized he seemed intoxicated—red eyes, very relaxed, probably drunk. He only spoke Spanish, so my dad helped translate. He claimed he braked hard because of a red light, but we were several cars back, not at the light itself. If I had called the police and reported the accident, would the fact that the other driver seemed drunk have made him at all responsible (even though I rear-ended him)? Not looking to pursue it further, just curious how liability works in this scenario if police had been called.

My girlfriend was hit by an uninsured driver while delivering mail for USPS in California—the other driver crossed the double yellow to pass and sideswiped her. The at-fault driver has no insurance but the truck is co-signed with her father. USPS can handle the legal claim but would take half of any settlement. Can my girlfriend handle the claim herself? What factors should she keep in mind regarding lost wages or pain and suffering?

Is it illegal in Arizona to stop in an intersection while waiting to turn left? Please cite the relevant statutes, particularly ARS 28-645 and ARS 28-873. I'd like elaboration supported by the law—does the law prohibit stopping in the intersection for a left turn, or is it permitted under certain circumstances? If possible, include any relevant credentials or experience interpreting Arizona traffic law. My understanding is you should only be in the intersection if you are directly ready to complete your turn.

Looking for guidance on using credit reports in pre-employment screening in New York State (excluding NYC). Specifically, after obtaining an applicant’s credit report, what negative credit factors may legally be used to disqualify someone? I’m familiar with NYC restrictions, the FCRA, NY Article 23-A, and EEOC protections for criminal background checks, but I can’t find clear criteria on using financial credit information for employment decisions in NY State. Can adverse action be taken for any job-relevant credit issue, as long as there’s no disparate impact on protected classes?

Suppose a 14 or 15 year old makes an Instagram account and posts images of a much younger-looking child—either edited photos of themselves or random photos from the internet. The goal is to attract adults with inappropriate intentions. After forming a connection with these adults, the teen tells them about a personal issue (like dry skin and not having access to moisturizer), and one of the adults offers to send a gift online to "help." Once the item is received, the teen stops communicating.

Is it illegal for the teen to do this? Would the teen face any criminal or civil liability for impersonating a younger child, soliciting gifts, or scamming these adults in this context? Or would the adult be unable to pursue any legal action because of their intent or actions interacting with a minor? Does any aspect of this situation count as fraud or a scam under the law?

Seeking advice for Missouri (MO): My former apartment complex is charging me ~$300 for carpet replacement and a fridge handle, claiming “excessive animal urine” after I moved out. I left the apartment clean (except for a broken fridge handle which I reported), did not cause carpet damage, and my dog never urinated indoors. They never contacted me for a walkthrough, have no photo evidence, and when I inspected the unit with my girlfriend, there was only a fresh paint and carpet smell—no trace of urine. Both the property and regional managers insist the smell was “overwhelming,” but they cannot show me any damage and there’s no documentation. They’re demanding payment by tomorrow or they’ll send me to collections. Should I pay and then sue in small claims to recover my deposit, or is there a better course of action? Any advice welcome.

I’m in Massachusetts and thinking about breaking my lease due to the landlord not making necessary repairs. Lease is up at the end of August, but we’ve had major unresolved issues—leaks (one ongoing for 10+ days, one from December that revealed lots of existing water damage), severe heating problems (never above 62°F, landlord just offers a space heater, electrical issues), and a broken/sticking front door that’s worsened the draft. Maintenance is always bare minimum and often just delays or ignores problems. I’ve documented everything with photos, correspondence, and logs and have informed the landlord via certified letter that we may withhold rent if repairs aren’t made, and plan to put March rent into escrow if things don’t improve by my deadline.

My questions:
1. Does a prior leak from December that left water damage (but isn’t actively leaking now) still count as an unresolved issue for the landlord’s repair timeline?
2. For the current leak, can I claim the landlord knowingly failed to repair it since before we moved in, based on past cover-ups and damage?
3. Regarding heat: if baseboard heat works but the apartment stays below code minimum and isn’t weather-tight, is this a 24-hour emergency repair or a 30-day structural issue?
4. Has the landlord already violated the warranty of habitability based on everything above, or should I wait a full 30 days from the most recent leak before taking action?
5. Is it risky to break the lease and move without going to court, especially if I need to sign a new lease elsewhere?
6. Should I expect anything when I call the city inspector, or is there anything I should do before involving them?
